symbols.name: digit width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each radix-2^d digit.
symbols.quote: Fix a digit width $d$, the number of bits in each digit, and a digit count $L$, the number of digits in each input, with $Ld \ge n$ so that both inputs fit.

symbols.name: digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of radix-2^d digits in each input.
symbols.quote: Fix a digit width $d$, the number of bits in each digit, and a digit count $L$, the number of digits in each input, with $Ld \ge n$ so that both inputs fit.

symbols.name: digit of x
symbols.meaning: The j-th radix-2^d digit of x, an integer in [0, 2^d), with index 0 the least significant.
symbols.quote: The digit $x_j$ is the $j$-th radix-$2^d$ digit of $x$, an integer in $[0, 2^d)$, with $x_0$ the least significant; $y_j$ is defined the same way from $y$.

symbols.name: digit of y
symbols.meaning: The j-th radix-2^d digit of y, defined in the same way as the digits of x.
symbols.quote: The digit $x_j$ is the $j$-th radix-$2^d$ digit of $x$, an integer in $[0, 2^d)$, with $x_0$ the least significant; $y_j$ is defined the same way from $y$.

symbols.name: indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the digit polynomials P(t) and Q(t).
symbols.quote: Digits become the coefficients of polynomials in a new indeterminate $t$, $P(t) = \sum_{j} x_j t^j$ and $Q(t) = \sum_{j} y_j t^j$, so that $P(2^d) = x$ and $Q(2^d) = y$.

symbols.name: digit polynomial of x
symbols.meaning: The polynomial in t whose coefficients are the digits x_j of x.
symbols.quote: Digits become the coefficients of polynomials in a new indeterminate $t$, $P(t) = \sum_{j} x_j t^j$ and $Q(t) = \sum_{j} y_j t^j$, so that $P(2^d) = x$ and $Q(2^d) = y$.

symbols.name: digit polynomial of y
symbols.meaning: The polynomial in t whose coefficients are the digits y_j of y.
symbols.quote: Digits become the coefficients of polynomials in a new indeterminate $t$, $P(t) = \sum_{j} x_j t^j$ and $Q(t) = \sum_{j} y_j t^j$, so that $P(2^d) = x$ and $Q(2^d) = y$.

symbols.name: convolution coefficient
symbols.meaning: The j-th coefficient of the product P(t)Q(t), the convolution of the two digit lists.
symbols.quote: The product $P(t)Q(t) = \sum_j e_j t^j$ has coefficients $e_j = \sum_{i+l=j} x_i y_l$, the convolution of the two digit lists, and so $xy = P(2^d)Q(2^d) = \sum_j e_j 2^{dj}$.

relations.quote: Radix-digit convolution reduces [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) to a convolution of short integer digit lists, which is the first step toward a fast product.
The convolution is computed by [transforms](discrete-fourier-transform.md) quickly on a fixed layout, which is why the reduction stops at this form rather than at the integer product.
